name: litmaps
description: Find research papers through the citation network, build Litmaps citation maps, and see them in the conversation.

interface.longDescription:
Litmaps helps you discover and organise academic literature using the citation network. Ask ChatGPT to find papers on a topic, explore everything related to a paper you already know, and see the results as an interactive Litmaps citation map: papers laid out by publication date and citation count, connected by their citations.

With Litmaps in ChatGPT you can:
- Search Litmaps' database of academic articles by keyword or DOI.
- Find related work for one or more papers using Litmaps' citation-connected ranking: papers that share citations and references with yours, including work that never cites them directly.
- Get a paper's full reference list or every paper that cites it.
- Find papers by authors your seed papers share.
- Check whether a paper has been retracted.
- Create maps in your Litmaps account, annotate them with labels and themed groups, and view them right in the conversation.
- Save papers to tags (collections) and your Read Later list.

Sign in with your Litmaps account to use your library. Maps are shown as they are in your account, and stay private. Editing, panning and zooming a map happen in the Litmaps app; the map in ChatGPT is a read-only view with a link to open it there.

Limitations: this app can't delete maps, tags or papers, or change account settings. The in-chat map uses Litmaps' standard layout (publication date by citations).
capabilities: Find related papers through the citation network
Get a paper's references or citing papers
Create and annotate Litmaps citation maps
Show interactive citation maps in the conversation
Organise papers into tags and Read Later
defaultPrompt: Show me a map of the most important papers on CRISPR base editing
Find papers related to "Attention Is All You Need" published since 2022
Has the paper with DOI 10.1038/nature14539 been retracted?

positive.description: Topic search shown as a Litmap: search results are drawn as an unsaved Litmap, not only listed.
positive.prompt: Find the most-cited recent papers on peroxiredoxin oxidation
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the most relevant results as an unsaved Litmap in the conversation (papers by publication date and citation count, linked by citations), with a short written summary of the highlights. Nothing is saved to the account.

positive.description: Related work: expand from a known paper through the citation network, shown as a Litmap.
positive.prompt: What papers are related to 'Attention Is All You Need'?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the paper, then shows the related papers (ranked by Litmaps' citation-connected ranking: sharing citations and references with it) as an unsaved Litmap with the seed paper marked, plus a short written summary. Nothing is saved to the account.

positive.description: Save a Litmap: when asked to keep it, the Litmap is saved to the user's account and shown.
positive.prompt: Make a Litmap of the key CRISPR base editing papers and save it to my account
positive.expected_behavior: Saves a Litmap of the key papers in the reviewer's workspace and draws it in the conversation, with an Open in Litmaps button that opens the saved Litmap.

positive.description: Single-paper question: a retraction check is answered in text, without a Litmap.
positive.prompt: Has the paper with DOI 10.1038/nature14539 been retracted?
positive.expected_behavior: States that the paper ("Deep learning", LeCun, Bengio and Hinton, 2015) has not been retracted. No Litmap is shown, since it's about one paper.

positive.description: Grow a saved Litmap: follow-on papers are added to the user's existing Litmap and it's shown again, rather than listed.
positive.prompt: Find follow-on papers published since 2023 that build on the papers in my CRISPR Litmap, add the best ones to it, and show it
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the reviewer's CRISPR Litmap, finds later work connected to its papers, adds the most relevant (typically 5 to 15) to that same Litmap, and shows the updated Litmap with a short note on what was added and why. It doesn't reply with only a list or create a separate Litmap.

negative.description: Unrelated request: no Litmaps tools should be called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Auckland tomorrow?

negative.description: Unsupported destructive action: no tool is called; ChatGPT explains that the Litmaps app can't delete maps and suggests doing it in the Litmaps web app.
Ambiguous target: with several Litmaps in the account, ChatGPT lists them (list_workspaces, list_litmaps) and asks which one to use before adding anything.
negative.prompt: Add these papers to my Litmap: 10.1038/nature14539 and 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762

publication.release_notes: Litmaps shown in conversations from before the tools were renamed draw again. get_map_graph returns as a view-only alias of get_litmap_graph, which the Litmap view in those conversations calls, and the current view also reads show_map's earlier results. The model never sees get_map_graph, and no other tool changes.
